newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa product exports drop in March.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa product exports drop in March.

text.p: Ivory Coast's semi-finished cocoa product and powder exports fell to 6,530 tonnes in March from 8,830 tonnes in February, official shipping data showed.

Cumulative exports in the first six months of the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season -- including those from October 1 to October 24 when the season opened -- were 47,233 tonnes, against 32,111 tonnes in 1995/96.

The figures do not separate liquor, butter and cake exports but powder shipments from Abidjan totalled 687 tonnes. Cumulative powder shipments were 3,314 tonnes this season against 2,578 the year before and just 49 in 1994/95.
Ivory Coast's cocoa bean processing capacity of 160,000 tonnes is set to rise in 1997/98 as the government encourages investors to build processing plants to add export value.
Port sources said local factory purchases of cocoa beans in 1996/97 (to April 25) totalled 86,000 tonnes, with around 44,000 tonnes taken by Callebaut-Barry's two SACO factories.
Abidjan-based processors Chocodi and Unicao took a total of about 32,000 tonnes. Stocks of unshipped products remain in some factory warehouses.
